title: Async prefix primer + Bloom-filter hinting for tokenizer fast-path
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Reduce prefill CPU overhead and tail latency for common short-prefix workloads by introducing an async prefix primer combined with a lightweight Bloom-filter based cache hint. The goal is to (1) detect hot prefixes quickly without blocking the main prefill path, (2) pre-warm KV/cache or kernel selection hints asynchronously for likely next tokens, and (3) skip expensive normalization/segmentation for known ASCII-heavy prefixes using a validated fast-path. Success metrics: 10-20% lower median prefill CPU, 15% lower p95 prefill latency for <256-token requests, and no regressions on long-tail Unicode-heavy inputs. This ticket covers the design, a proof-of-concept implementation in the prefill worker, a small canary rollout, and telemetry to validate coverage and regressions.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Async primer added to prefill worker with non-blocking backpressure. 2) Bloom filter stores compact signature of hot prefixes; hits trigger kernel/hint pre-warm but do not change correctness. 3) Fast-path for ASCII prefixes bypasses heavy normalization and is guarded by a safety timeout. 4) CI includes unit tests and fuzz inputs covering multi-byte boundaries. 5) Canary rollout shows target metrics without increasing error rate or decoding discrepancies.
implementation_notes: - Add a small async queue keyed by (customer_id, route, prefix_hash) with dedup TTL. - Bloom filter per-worker with 8e4 entries, serialized to memory-mapped state for fast cold-start. - On bloom-hit, emit a non-blocking pre-warm event: allocate KV cache and enqueue kernel selection hints in the kernel router. - Fast-path uses lightweight ASCII tokenizer inlined in the prefill hotlane; fall back to full tokenizer if uncertain. - Metrics: prefix_hit_rate, async_prewarm_latency, fastpath_fallback_rate, p95_prefill_latency.
risks_and_mitigation: - False positives in Bloom filter could waste pre-warm resources: mitigate with conservative sizing and cost-aware throttling. - Async pre-warms may cause bursty CPU; add token-bucket admission and customer-level max concurrent pre-warms. - Fast-path could introduce subtle tokenization differences; add deterministic equivalence tests and enable fast-path behind a rollout flag per-route.
testing_plan: - Unit tests for bloom signatures, TTL dedup, and ascii fast-path correctness. - Integration test that simulates common prefixes and verifies kernel hint is observed in router logs. - Canary on dedicated capacity group with 1% traffic, extended to 10% based on no regressions. - Synthetic benchmark comparing baseline vs PR on short prompt p50/p95 and CPU utilization.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag gated default-off; internal dev environment smoke tests. 2) Canary: enable for small subset of routes/customers (1%). 3) Observe metrics for 48h and run rollback if error_rate > 0.1% or p95 latency regresses > 5%. 4) Ramp to 10% then 50% and full release tied to runtime-1.19 patch window.
